jokes.label: Joke A
jokes.title: Not on My Watch
jokes.joke: I used to work as a paramedic. One night, a guy on a stretcher grabbed my arm and said, 'Be honest with me. Am I going to die?' I looked him straight in the eye and said, 'Nobody dies on my watch.' He said, 'Okay, when does your shift end?'

jokes.label: Joke B
jokes.title: Exit Interview
jokes.joke: I got laid off last month, and they were really nice about it. They walked me out with a box of my stuff, a handshake, and a sad little speech. Honestly, I’ve been to funerals with less ceremony. The difference is, at a funeral nobody asks you to return your badge. And at least the guy in the mausoleum doesn’t have to update his LinkedIn.

jokes.label: Joke C
jokes.title: First Responder
jokes.joke: I realized I could never be an emergency medical responder because I’m way too vindictive. If you cut me off in traffic, and two miles later I find your car wrapped around a telephone pole... I'll still give you CPR. But I'm doing the chest compressions to the beat of 'Baby Shark'. And I'm going to make sure you wake up during the 'doo-doo-doo' part.

jokes.label: Joke D
jokes.title: The Long Way
jokes.joke: I'm an emergency medical responder, and I try to stay professional, but sometimes I get a little vindictive. Last week this guy who cut me off in traffic was having a panic attack. I leaned over and whispered, 'Breathe into this bag... of all the things you should've considered before that left turn.'

jokes.label: Joke E
jokes.title: Performance Review
jokes.joke: I told my boss, "I want brutally honest feedback." He said, "Okay, if a customer kidnapped you, we'd call back and ask what your ransom demands are." I said, "Wow, that's hard to hear." He goes, "Good news: after today, you won't hear it from your boss anymore."

scores.comment: Clear first-person setup, but the funeral comparison is predictable and the LinkedIn punchline feels familiar. More observational than laugh-inducing.
Strong comic premise with a recognizable annoyance and a nicely escalating revenge fantasy. The final Baby Shark detail delivers a distinct, visual punchline. Good stage potential.
The premise has potential, but the bag wordplay is awkward and linguistically forced. The punchline sacrifices conversational plausibility for a clever-sounding construction.

The ransom comparison is an amusing exaggeration, and the firing provides a second turn. Clear and economical, though the final reveal is somewhat predictable once the boss becomes aggressively candid.
Clean stage premise and a tidy turn: the dying patient only wants to know when the paramedic’s shift ends. The structure is familiar, but the timing is tight and the last line carries the laugh.

Strong concrete image: vindictive CPR timed to Baby Shark, with the guy waking up for the ‘doo-doo-doo’. It escalates well and fits the two seeds. The opening ‘could never be’ logic is slightly loose, and the ending runs a bit long.
The vindictive-paramedic premise is clear, but the punchline is garbled. ‘Breathe into this bag... of all the things’ doesn’t land as a turn, and the real insult is buried.

The ‘brutally honest feedback’ setup is familiar, and the ransom-demand line is confusing and doesn’t read as feedback. The firing twist at the end is the only real turn, and it isn’t set up well enough to snap.
Clean execution and solid rhythm, but relies on a somewhat familiar and predictable street-joke trope.
Good natural stand-up voice with relatable observations, though comparing a layoff to a funeral is a fairly standard angle.
The situational coincidence strains credibility for a believable stage anecdote, and the punchline phrasing feels a bit forced.
Strong escalation with a snappy double-punchline that delivers a satisfying snap while naturally weaving in the concepts.
Clean misdirect and tight timing; familiar medical structure keeps it from higher marks.
Serviceable layoff-funeral parallel but soft, multi-beat payoff with little snap.
Clear premise, specific petty image, and well-timed final detail carry a real laugh.
Clever feedback analogy and clean firing turn, but overall mild rather than sharp.
Strong misdirection, clean dialogue, and a punchline that lands naturally.
Clear premise with relatable comparisons, but the turns are fairly expected and familiar.
Funny central image, but the setup is long and the ending repeats the same idea rather than escalating it.
Premise is understandable, but the punchline feels strained and doesn't deliver a strong comedic turn.
